description: 32x24 RGB/8; a base layer with a clipped layer above it (clipping flag set).

expectationSource.method: psd-tools PSDImage.open() for structure and layer records; composite() for compositePixels; layer.numpy() for layerPixels. No Agogo code in the loop.
manualChecks: compositePixels is deliberately NOT asserted for this fixture. The sidecar's composite samples come from psd-tools re-rendering the layer stack, and Agogo renders it too; those are two different renderers. Where the stack is plain source-over they agree (every other fixture asserts compositePixels and passes), but this fixture exists precisely to exercise semantics where two renderers are not obliged to agree pixel-for-pixel. Per-layer rasters are still asserted via layerPixels, which is unambiguous. Comparing renderers here would assert that Agogo matches psd-tools' arithmetic, which is not the contract. Clipping-group compositing differs between implementations.

writer.lossyReason: PLAN.md S.10.2: psdexport emits layer channels in its own fixed order (0,1,2,-1; gray 0,-1) and always emits an alpha channel, because the engine model is RGBA. This fixture was authored with alpha first (-1,0,1,2) or with no alpha channel at all, so every re-exported record's channelIds differ in order and the flattened records gain a -1. The PSD spec does not prescribe channel order and readers key on the ID, so this is a spelling difference rather than lost data. Allowlisting a path suppresses the WHOLE assertion, so this entry on its own would also excuse a dropped -2 user mask or a corrupted ID; it does not, because the ID set is asserted separately at psdRecords[N].channelIds.preserved, which is emitted strictly and which no writer.lossy entry can reach. That path permits exactly one gained channel, the alpha psdexport always writes, and nothing else. psd-tools 1.19.0 reads the re-export correctly; ImageMagick was not installed when this file's bytes were last re-verified, so this fixture rests on one independent reader rather than two (see testdata/VERIFICATION.md).

externalVerification.notes: tools/psdfixtures/verify_dump.py re-read the Agogo re-export with psd-tools 1.19.0 after the S.10.3/S.10.4 writer fix changed the bytes Agogo writes for masked and clipped layers; the file was accepted and reported the expected structure and bounds. This run used psd-tools alone - ImageMagick was not installed in the re-verification environment - so this row rests on one independent reader rather than two. See testdata/VERIFICATION.md.
